description: Reference dictionary for all wiggle perturbation tactics: mechanism, applicability, and truth-value semantics.

truth_value_key.true: The perturbed statement is always mathematically true (provable from Mathlib).
truth_value_key.false: The perturbed statement is always mathematically false (refutable).
truth_value_key.unknown: Truth cannot be determined without a proof search; may be true or false.
truth_value_key.chain_broken: A step in the chain returned no output (tactic not applicable to that statement).

chain_composition_rule.description: How is_true values are composed when perturbations are chained.

rules.reason: Two consecutive false-labelled steps may cancel (e.g. negate -> negate recovers the original statement).
A single false step makes the whole chain false (unless cancelled by another false step as above).

chain_composition_rule.precedence: False+False=unknown takes priority; then False dominates; then unknown dominates; True only if all steps are True.

perturbations.name: negate
perturbations.mechanism: Reverts all hypotheses into the goal, then wraps the full statement in negation (not P). The Lean tactic pushes the negation inward with push_neg.
perturbations.is_true_reason: The negation of a true theorem is always false.
perturbations.output_form: Lean extracted theorem string (theorem wiggle_demo.extracted... := sorry)
perturbations.notes: push_neg converts ¬∀ to ∃ and ¬(a > b) to a ≤ b, so the output is usually in prenex form.

perturbations.name: contrapose
perturbations.mechanism: Applies the contrapositive transformation: rewrites P → Q as ¬Q → ¬P. Uses simp with ← and_imp and contrapose internally.
perturbations.is_true_reason: The contrapositive is logically equivalent to the original; if the original is true, so is its contrapositive.
perturbations.applies_to: Implication statements (P → Q). Also works on iff (↔) statements by applying to both directions.
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Bare equalities, existential statements, or goals with no propositional structure.
perturbations.notes: For iff (P ↔ Q), the tactic rewrites to (¬P ↔ ¬Q), which is also logically equivalent.

perturbations.name: converse
perturbations.mechanism: Swaps hypothesis and conclusion: rewrites P → Q as Q → P.
perturbations.is_true_reason: The converse of a true implication may or may not hold. Example: the converse of a ≠ 0 → a * a⁻¹ = 1 asks whether a * a⁻¹ = 1 implies a ≠ 0, which is a separate question.
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Bare equalities, disjunctions, universally quantified statements without a top-level implication.
perturbations.notes: If the original was an iff (P ↔ Q), converse gives the same iff, so output equals input.

perturbations.name: drop_unused_hyp
perturbations.mechanism: Clears all Prop-valued hypotheses that do not appear in the goal (clear_unused_props tactic). Produces a more general statement with fewer premises.
perturbations.is_true_reason: Removing a hypothesis that was never used in the proof cannot invalidate the conclusion; the theorem remains provable without it.
perturbations.applies_to: Theorems that have at least one unused Prop hypothesis (e.g. a dummy h : True).
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Theorems where every hypothesis is used in the proof. Returns no output in that case.
perturbations.input_example: ∀ (x : ℝ) (h_unused : True), HasDerivAt Real.exp (Real.exp x) x
perturbations.notes: Only clears Prop hypotheses, not Type or data arguments. The canonical test case is a theorem with an explicit h : True parameter.

perturbations.name: tc_weaken_hyp
perturbations.mechanism: Replaces a typeclass in the hypothesis with a weaker parent class from the Mathlib hierarchy (e.g. [AddCommMonoid α] → [AddMonoid α]). Uses BFS up the _HARDCODED_PARENTS graph (depth=2), tries each ancestor, and keeps the first one that Lean type-checks.
perturbations.is_true_reason: A weaker hypothesis means the theorem must hold for a strictly LARGER class of types — i.e. the variant is a STRONGER claim than the original. The original proof relied on the strictly stronger structure (e.g. commutativity in AddCommMonoid) and no longer applies. Whether the variant is still true depends on the specific theorem; e.g. a + b = b + a fails in a general AddMonoid (string concatenation).
perturbations.applies_to: Theorems with a typeclass in square brackets [TC α] where TC has a parent in the hardcoded hierarchy.
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Theorems with no bracket typeclass (e.g. plain Nat theorems), or where no weaker parent compiles.
perturbations.input_example: ∀ {α} [AddCommMonoid α] (a b : α), a + b = b + a
perturbations.output_example: ∀ {α} [AddMonoid α] (a b : α), a + b = b + a
perturbations.output_form: Clean ∀-type string (not a Lean extracted theorem)
perturbations.notes: Compiled with `example : <type> := by sorry` to confirm the weaker class provides all required operations. The compile check only verifies WELL-TYPEDNESS, NOT provability — so a passing variant may still be mathematically false. Uses typeclass_mutate.weaken_hypothesis_typeclass.

perturbations.name: tc_strengthen_hyp
perturbations.mechanism: Replaces a typeclass in the hypothesis with a stronger child class (e.g. [AddCommMonoid α] → [AddCommGroup α]). BFS down the children graph.
perturbations.is_true_reason: A stronger hypothesis restricts the domain of applicability, but the conclusion still holds for any type that satisfies the stronger requirement (since it also satisfies the original).
perturbations.applies_to: Theorems with a typeclass in square brackets [TC α] where TC has a known child class.
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Leaf nodes in the hierarchy (e.g. NormedField, LinearOrderedField) that have no children.
perturbations.input_example: ∀ {α} [AddCommMonoid α] (a b : α), a + b = b + a
perturbations.output_example: ∀ {α} [AddCommGroup α] (a b : α), a + b = b + a
perturbations.notes: Uses typeclass_mutate.strengthen_hypothesis_typeclass. The variant is a WEAKER statement (fewer types qualify) but remains true.

perturbations.name: tc_strengthen_conc
perturbations.mechanism: Replaces a Prop-valued typeclass in the conclusion with a stronger child class (e.g. IsDomain → EuclideanDomain). Operates on the conclusion text after the last top-level comma or →.
perturbations.is_true_reason: Claiming a stronger structural property than the original may or may not follow from the hypotheses. Example: IsDomain (Polynomial R) → EuclideanDomain (Polynomial R) is not generally true.
perturbations.applies_to: Theorems whose conclusion is or contains a Prop-valued typeclass application (e.g. IsDomain T, IsField T).
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Theorems with equality or inequality conclusions, or whose conclusion typeclass has no known children.
perturbations.notes: Uses _PROP_TC_PARENTS (separate from _HARDCODED_PARENTS) which tracks Prop-valued predicates like IsDomain, IsField, Nontrivial.

perturbations.name: tc_weaken_conc
perturbations.mechanism: Replaces a Prop-valued typeclass in the conclusion with a weaker parent (e.g. IsDomain → Nontrivial). BFS up the _PROP_TC_PARENTS graph.
perturbations.is_true_reason: If the original conclusion TC holds, then any weaker parent TC' also holds (by definition of the hierarchy). The original proof implies the weaker version.
perturbations.applies_to: Theorems whose conclusion contains a Prop-valued typeclass that has a parent in _PROP_TC_PARENTS.
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Equality/inequality conclusions, or root nodes in _PROP_TC_PARENTS with no parents.

perturbations.name: flip_bound
perturbations.mechanism: Finds the first inequality symbol in the type_str and reverses its direction: ≥ ↔ ≤, > ↔ <. Pure regex substitution on the string; no Lean compilation.
perturbations.is_true_reason: Reversing an inequality can make a true statement false (n > 0 → n < 0 is impossible for ℕ), or can leave it true (a ≤ b ∨ b ≤ a reversed to a ≥ b ∨ b ≤ a remains a valid comparability claim). Must be checked case by case.
perturbations.applies_to: Any theorem whose type_str contains ≥, ≤, >, or <.
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Theorems with only equalities (=), disequalities (≠), or no comparison operators.
perturbations.notes: Only the FIRST matching inequality is flipped. Search order is ≥, ≤, >, < — so ≥ is flipped before > if both are present. Defined in bounds.py.

perturbations.name: bound_tighter
perturbations.mechanism: Finds the first inequality followed immediately by a numeric literal and shifts that literal in the tighter direction: ≥n → ≥(n+1), ≤n → ≤(n-1), >n → >(n+1), <n → <(n-1). Clamps to 0 so negatives are avoided.
perturbations.is_true_reason: Tightening a bound in a hypothesis restricts the domain (theorem still true but narrower); tightening in a conclusion claims more (often false). Cannot be determined without proof search.
perturbations.applies_to: Theorems whose type_str contains an inequality (≥, ≤, >, <) immediately followed by a non-negative integer literal.
perturbations.does_not_apply_to: Theorems where all inequalities are between variables (e.g. k + m < k + n has no numeric literal after <). Theorems with only =, ≠.
perturbations.notes: Only the FIRST matching inequality+literal pair is shifted. Search order matches tightening semantics: ≥ first, then ≤, then >, then <. Defined in bounds.py.
